verdict.rationale: Blink Shell is itself a first-party command-line shell. It ships built-in commands such as ssh, mosh, curl, scp/sftp, config and file utilities, and it supports simple python/lua scripting with redirection, though without pipes. Nothing in the evidence ties it to AI-native or agentic workflows, and the llms.txt and OpenAPI probes both returned 404. missing for 10: any AI/agent-oriented CLI usage or docs, machine-readable output or automation hooks for agents, pipe support, independent corroboration of CLI use for automation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: Using Blink Shell is similar to most other terminals - you simply type commands and hit the `RETURN` key.
Manage and edit files from the command line, check on your network or download files.
You can call commands individually, or use small scripts using python or lua. There is redirection (">", "<", "&>" ...), but no pipe.
cat, grep, wc, cd, setenv, ls, touch, cp, rm, ln, mv, mkdir, rmdir, df, du
